faq.q: What is the minimum down payment in Canada?
faq.a: 5% on homes of $500,000 or less; on homes between $500,000 and $1,499,999, 5% on the first $500,000 plus 10% on the portion over $500,000; at $1,500,000 or more, a minimum of 20% — and mortgage loan insurance is not available at that level.

faq.q: When do I need mortgage loan insurance, and what does it cost?
faq.a: Whenever your down payment is under 20% on a home priced at $1.5 million or less. CMHC publishes premium rates ranging from 0.6% to 4.5% of the total mortgage amount, depending on the down payment size and loan amount; the premium can be paid up front or added to the mortgage.

faq.q: How much of my income can go to housing and debt?
faq.a: FCAC's guidelines: total monthly housing costs (mortgage payments, property taxes, heating, 50% of condo fees) should not exceed 39% of gross household income (GDS), and total debt load including all other debts should not exceed 44% (TDS); slightly higher ratios may still qualify but carry more risk.
